text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers are accurate and match the card and tool outputs (26.8% vs 3.0%, 46%, 0 of 30 below, 6 of 19 data-without-tests, 0 of 9 99215 documented below). Language is mostly cautious and the leaning of inconclusive is reasonable. But the summary is internally inconsistent and has weaknesses: the headline says '20% of notes' while the body uses 6 of 19 and 6 of 30, and the 20% is a share of all 30 charts, not of notes claiming data review. The 'notes may have been written up to match the bill' line is speculative and sits uneasily with charts that support the billed level. The cited examples are only two low-complexity claims, with no high-complexity contrast or flagged documented 99215 claims, and they are not tied to the data-review issue. The next steps ask for more records, yet 30 of 30 usable charts were returned and the 'too thin' claim is weak. They also do not name the 6 claims with unmatched data review for a targeted audit. Mentioning that the 99215s are high for low-complexity patients is useful, but the main anomaly goes unexplored: documentation supports high MDM even where the patients have few conditions.","problems":["Headline '20% of notes' conflates 6/30 charts with the 6/19 subset of notes claiming data review; inconsistent denominators.","Speculation that notes were 'written up to match the bill' is not well supported and conflicts with the finding that charts support billed levels.","Next steps are generic: no list of the 6 claims with unmatched data review, and no request for specific documentation for the cited low-complexity 99215 claims.","Cited examples (C0096603, C0096616) are not shown to be among the documented charts or tied to the data-review finding; no high-complexity contrast.","Does not reconcile the high 99215 share in low-complexity patients with documentation supporting high MDM (e.g. C0096676 documented high MDM with only obesity).","Says records are too thin even though 30 of 30 charts were usable, with only 9 documented 99215 claims; the reasoning on sample adequacy is not explained."]}
